findings.summary: The plan treats the introspector as unbuilt and request-only, but it exists in code and in the docs.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs lines 1-15: 'After each of these events, Athena records one introspection ... a job that ends rejected or failed ...', and it asks Jev 'the failure-class and is-repeat questions'. A grep for 'introspect' matches 48 files, including docs/design/defaults-loop.md, roles-and-ladder.md, scope-guard.md and requirements-map.md. The plan says 'A grep of docs/ finds no file naming the introspector'. Fix: In step 1, read introspect.rs and defaults-loop.md sections 3.1-3.4. In the 'what exists today' table, list the introspector as built, citing introspect.rs and the athena.introspection/1 schema. Describe the relation as built on the existing record, not on an assumed interface.
findings.location: Plan decision 2 reason; criterion 4 demonstration; risk 1

findings.summary: The proposed post-mortem overlaps the existing introspection step and failure classes, and the plan does not say whether it extends that step or replaces it.
findings.evidence: The introspection step already fires on rejected and failed jobs and classifies failures. The new step has the same triggers plus planning-stopped. Failure classes already appear in docs/records.md, records.rs, steward.rs and proposals.rs. Fix: Design the post-mortem as an extension of the introspection record: add the planning-stopped trigger and a 'context that would have prevented it' field with the fixed outcome classes. Do not create a separate recorded step. In D130, give the alternative 'separate post-mortem record' and why it was rejected. Make build job 4's acceptance test exercise the existing introspection path.

findings.summary: The requirements engineer is called absent, but BRIEF.md proposes it.
findings.evidence: BRIEF.md line 1010: '4A. Athena gets a requirements engineer. It owns the spec and the shared vocabulary ...'. BRIEF.md line 1085 also has the 2026-10-26 addendum 'Jev checks for code health'. Fix: Cite BRIEF.md 4A as the source: the role is proposed there and not built. Since that role owns the spec and the vocabulary, state who owns what between the two roles.

findings.summary: The reading names roles-and-ladder.md as a doc to check for a mapping conflict, but step 1 does not read it.
findings.evidence: The reading's assumptions say 'The designer checks docs/design/hestia.md and roles-and-ladder.md'. docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md exists and covers the plan-stage audit and introspections. Step 1 lists BRIEF.md, hestia.md, requirements-map.md, scope-guard.md and ontology.toml only. Fix: Add roles-and-ladder.md to step 1 and record the mapping call against it.

findings.summary: Most demonstrations run `git diff` and then rely on reading the doc, which is expected for a content job but weak.
findings.evidence: Every 'Run:' line is git diff or git diff --stat. Fix: Where possible, add a grep check, for example that every row of the conventions table contains 'mechanism:' or 'prose-only', so the check is mechanical.

summary: The plan's structure is sound: it is docs-only, uses the right four files, gives D130 the D129 format, labels its numbers, plans to re-measure them, and splits the build into six jobs with failing-case-first bullets. But it rests on a false premise. Decision 2, criterion 4's demonstration and the risk mitigation all say no file names the introspector, so the design would mark it "not present in the snapshot (request-only)". In fact crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs exists. After each job that ends rejected or failed, it already records an introspection and asks Jev a failure-class question. Many design docs describe it as well. So the proposed post-mortem (decision 3) partly duplicates a step that is already built, and the plan never reconciles the two. That would make the design wrong on criteria 2 and 4. A smaller fix: the requirements engineer is proposed in BRIEF.md (decision sheet item 4A, line 1010), so the plan should cite that rather than calling it absent. I checked this by grepping and reading the snapshot.
